issue: Is a Rule 60(b) motion that adds a new claim, filed while an appeal from the denial of an initial federal habeas petition is still pending, a second or successive habeas petition under 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)?

sides.position: A Rule 60(b) motion filed while an appeal from the denial of an initial habeas petition is pending is a second or successive habeas petition under § 2244(b), so the district court lacks jurisdiction without authorization from the circuit.
A Rule 60(b) motion filed while an appeal from the denial of an initial habeas petition is pending is not a second or successive petition under § 2244(b).
cases: Ching v. United States, 298 F.3d 174 (2d Cir. 2002)
United States v. Santarelli, 929 F.3d 95 (3d Cir. 2019)

this_court: The majority holds the motion is a second or successive petition, following Beaty; the concurrence agrees only because Beaty binds the panel and writes to disagree with it.
quote: I write separately to register my disagreement with Beaty and to urge the Supreme Court to recognize the circuit split and to adopt the rule stated in Ching v. United States, 298 F.3d 174, 178 (2d Cir. 2002), and United States v. Santarelli, 929 F.3d 95, 104–05 (3d Cir. 2019).
cite: Alexander Balbuena v. William Sullivan, 980 F.3d 619 (9th Cir. 2020)
